title: Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift in Global Markets: Evidence from an Information Shock
one_line: When reporting quality improved sharply for non-US firms (an exogenous information shock), PEAD declined — more so where attention was less split, institutions owned more and arbitrage was easier — supporting limited attention as the cause of PEAD.

findings.statement: PEAD declines after the information shock.
Decline larger with fewer concurrent announcements, more institutions, lower limits to arbitrage.

reported_results.headline: When reporting quality improved sharply for non-US firms (an exogenous information shock), PEAD declined — more so where attention was less split, institutions owned more and arbitrage was easier — supporting limited attention as the cause of PEAD.

data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 4), not by the weekly pipeline.
